main_body: Three-storey brick building: a large flat paved roof seen from above, a cream cornice, then a brick facade with 3 rows of windows and a green arched double door
top_band: Lavender-grey roof surface, rows 1-40 at x=80. A light parapet edge sits on rows 1-2, textured slab rows 7-37 (L=168), and a light front-edge line on rows 38-40 (L=189-235)
evidence: The column scan shows a big horizontal roof surface with slab joints and two roof props (a chimney and a vent). It ends in a bright front-edge line (rows 39-40, L=235) and a cream cornice, then a dark band that works as eave shadow. Below that is the brick front face with windows, sills, lintels and an arched door. Both the roof top and the front face are clearly drawn and separated by a large tone step. The roof is a flat roof rather than a sloped one, but it reads as a real horizontal surface. The windows are only mildly recessed, with frames and sills.

style.evidence: Median colours per tile is 12, at or above the stone reference (11) and below the richer house (18). Flat-fill coverage is 0% and the dark edge pixels are 0% neutral, so the outlines are tinted (dark brown beside brick). The roof has about 5 lightness steps with speckle and slab joints. The brick has mortar variation and several tones, and the windows carry glass highlights. The total of 38 distinct colours is low next to the references, and the repeated identical windows are a little mechanical. Per-tile richness and craft are still on par with the reference.
